aiMl.flowTitle: How the forecast model is layered (read this once)
aiMl.flowBody:
1) DATA INGEST
   ThemeParks / canonical messages → wait times & status.

2) FEATURE STORE (5 min buckets)
   park_feature_snapshots_5m + ride_feature_snapshots_5m
   → calendar (holidays), weather, staffing gap, crowd proxy, etc.

3) BASELINE FORECAST
   Trend from recent snapshots + optional “Forecast influence factors”
   (Integrations → aiForecastFactors: weight / value / lag).

4) X-SNAPSHOT HEURISTIC LAYER
   applyXLayerToForecast → nudges +15/+60 from snapshot context
   (rain, holidays, traffic, staffing…). Source often FEATURE_SNAPSHOT_BASELINE_X_V1.

5) ENTERPRISE ML LAYER (L1 / L2 / L3)
   L1 = ml_global_factors (this page)
   L2 = ml_park_factors per park (X-Park-Id)
   L3 = ml_profiles + asset assignment + overrides
   → mergeMlEnterpriseLayer on top of step 4. May set forecastSource to FEATURE_MODEL.
   Dynamic L1 factor codes (e.g. holiday, weekend, school break, rain, summer, macro): “Current” is often resolved at merge time from `park_calendar_context`, `weather_observations`, and the snapshot timestamp/time zone when neither an L2 `current_value` nor an L1 API feed applies. Forecast JSON also includes `mlFactorCurrents` per code (`current`, `currentSource`, `calculatedCurrent`, …).

6) API / UI
   Ride grid & explanations consume the merged result.

Editing L1 here needs permission ai · refresh (not only ai · read).
aiMl.globalEditHint: View only: editing global factors requires permission ai · refresh on your user/role. Ask an admin to grant it, or use the API PATCH /api/v1/ai/global-factors/:id with a token that has ai.refresh.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How operational data flows into features, forecasts, and the AI screens in Smart Park OS.

overview.title: Data flow: park-wide vs per-asset
paragraphs: Smart Park OS connects vendor adapters and internal services into one operational picture. Distinct paths matter for ML: some signals describe the whole gate (weather, crowd proxies, park-level staffing gaps), while others belong to a single asset (ride queue, restaurant throughput, show capacity).

About every five minutes the platform materializes rolling buckets in the feature store. Park-wide rows capture context that is not tied to one ride ID. Per-asset rows attach to attractions, shows, restaurants, or shops when those integrations are configured.
Downstream forecasting combines both: entity models use their own history and, when available, the latest park snapshot as shared context so predictions stay coherent across the estate.

adapters.title: Integrations & adapters
paragraphs: Adapters normalize external payloads into the platform model. UNS topics, device connectors, and batch imports all funnel into the same canonical entities your operators see in Live Ops and master data.

Before trusting ML outputs, verify pipeline health: Devices & Services for credentials and endpoints, Adapter Operations for ingress logs, and UNS for topic structure. Broken ingress shows up first as missing or stale features, not as a broken chart axis.

snapshots.title: Five-minute snapshots & feature store
paragraphs: The feature store rolls operational signals into five-minute snapshot rows. Park snapshots aggregate gate-level signals (for example weather, traffic proxies, staffing hints). Entity snapshots carry ride/show/restaurant-specific fields such as waits, utilization, or staffing gaps tied to an asset id.

AI Studio lets you inspect how those rows look for the active park—useful when debugging surprising forecasts. Feature Store Monitor watches ingestion continuity; Feature Data Quality highlights incomplete rows, profile mismatches, and hygiene issues across park and entity tables.

completeness.title: Completeness score (0–1)
paragraphs: Completeness is a per-row diagnostic between 0 and 1. A value near 1 means the configured fields for that bucket are present and valid; lower values indicate missing weather, traffic, staffing, neighbor context, or other expected dimensions.
Use completeness to prioritize data fixes and adapter work—it is not a guest-facing KPI. A temporarily lower score during a partial outage is expected until sources recover.

forecast.title: Forecast pipeline (baseline → X-layer → ML)
paragraphs: Forecasts are computed on read in a fixed order (ADR 0001): (1) Baseline from recent 5m snapshot series plus integration configs `aiForecastFactors`, (2) snapshot-driven X heuristics from the latest park/ride rows, (3) enterprise ML adjustments from database factors and profiles.

Park snapshots supply shared context; ride snapshots supply entity waits and staffing. Refreshes rebuild features and scoring—purging snapshots requires ai · refresh in addition to ai · read. See the next section for where each parameter level is stored and which level wins.

factorLevels.title: Parameter levels, data flow, and precedence
paragraphs: Operational data always flows: adapters → System-of-Record tables → 5-minute park and ride feature snapshots → Forecast API. Configuration does not replace that path; it steers how the numeric forecast is adjusted once snapshot inputs exist.

On each forecast response the backend applies, in order: Baseline (time-series trend + integration factors) → X snapshot heuristic layer (fixed rules using weather, calendar, traffic, staffing, capacity from snapshots) → Enterprise ML layer (global DB factors, park overrides, then per-asset profile effects). Each stage consumes the previous stage’s output.

Baseline integration factors — one platform-wide list in Integrations (`aiForecastFactors`, edited via AI Insights / Integrations). Each row has scope PARK or ENTITY: park forecasts use only PARK-scoped rows; entity forecasts use PARK-scoped and ENTITY-scoped rows together. There is no separate JSON per park; you differentiate with scopes and extra rows.

Snapshot X-layer — not a weight table in the DB. The same coded rules run for every tenant, driven by the latest `park_feature_snapshots_5m` and `ride_feature_snapshots_5m`. You influence it by fixing ingest and snapshot completeness, not via ML Global/Park factor screens.
Enterprise ML L1 — `ml_global_factors`: default weight/value per factor code for the ML bump after the X-layer.

Enterprise ML L2 — `ml_park_factors` per park: for the same factor code, park `weightOverride` and `currentValue` take precedence over the global row when set; otherwise the global row applies. That is the “more specific level leads” rule for these codes.

Dynamically resolved “Current” (L1/L2): For selected global factor codes (e.g. HOLIDAY_PRESSURE, WEEKEND_UPLIFT, RAIN_DEMAND_SHIFT, SUMMER_SEASON_FACTOR, MACRO_TOURISM_INDEX), the merge layer often derives the effective multiplier from feature-store context instead of only the static L1 table cell. Precedence stays: L2 `current_value` > L1 row with `source_type` API > calculated (calendar/weather/time) > L1 `current_value`/default. Forecast responses include `mlFactorCurrents` with `currentSource` (e.g. L2_MANUAL, API, CALCULATED, L1_DEFAULT) so clients can explain the number.

Enterprise ML L3 — effective profile per asset (`ml_profiles` + `asset_ml_profile_assignments` with validity window, else defaults by asset type). `asset_ml_overrides` set per-asset keys that override profile defaults—asset-specific configuration wins over the raw profile.

Summary: for enterprise ML influence codes, specificity wins (Park over Global; asset overrides over profile defaults). Baseline integration factors follow PARK/ENTITY scope rules instead. The snapshot X-layer sits between baseline and ML and always runs from snapshot inputs.

aiScreens.title: AI Insights screens (what each is for)
paragraphs: AI Insights hub: live park forecast summary, factor editing (with Integrations · manage), and navigation into specialized tools.

Ride wait grid: compares live waits with short-horizon forecasts per asset. Timeseries: explores forecast horizons and overlays for a chosen ride. Accuracy: tracks error metrics over time to validate model health.

ML Global factors / ML Park factors / ML Profiles: configure weights, lags, and which explainable signals participate. Feature Store Monitor: operational view of feature ingestion. Feature Data Quality: audits snapshot hygiene; bulk delete and purge are gated behind ai · refresh.
AI Studio: experimentation surface—prompts, snapshot inspection, and tooling scoped to the active park for analysts and admins.

incidents.title: Incidents & assets
paragraphs: When creating or editing incidents, link the real attraction, restaurant, or show from platform assets. That keeps operational tickets aligned with the same external IDs used in features and forecasts, which improves traceability from a guest-facing issue back to ML context.

simulator.title: Simulator: demo lab & attraction OEE (MQTT)
paragraphs: The Simulator page has two separate tools. (1) Live simulator (demo): drives crowd/weather/ride demo flows via the API using fixed seeded zone and ride IDs—good for presentations without real MQTT. Start/stop/scenarios call POST /api/v1/simulator/start, …/stop, and …/scenario.

(2) Attraction OEE simulator: facility/ride operation only — it does not ingest or publish park weather or meteo feeds; use the demo simulator above for weather/crowd demos. Technically: one or more rides as OT/PLC-style Sparkplug on the API’s shared MQTT client (no second broker). Sparkplug B JSON-MVP: NBIRTH and per-device DBIRTH (device_id = attraction slug), then periodic DDATA with plant metrics (state, counters, capacity, queue, downtime hints, energy, etc.). Scenarios such as WEATHER_DELAY model an operational weather hold on the ride, not a weather service. Control: POST /api/v1/simulator/attraction-oee/start|stop|scenario; status: GET …/status. Requires MQTT_ENABLED=true and a reachable MQTT_BROKER_URL (e.g. mqtt://127.0.0.1:1883 locally, mqtt://mqtt:1883 in Docker Compose).

Optional environment tuning (see .env.example): SIM_OEE_* or shorthand SIM_* for park slug, edge node, publish interval, attraction list, scenario, and random seed. With SIM_OEE_ENABLED and SIM_OEE_AUTO_START the OEE simulator starts when the API process boots.

UNS Live labels this traffic as SIMULATED quality. To also subscribe UNS Live to NBIRTH/NDEATH/STATE patterns, set MQTT_SPARKPLUG_LIVE_SUBSCRIBE_ADVANCED=true (default subscriptions already include DDATA/DBIRTH/DDEATH). Platform OEE / downtime bookings remain separate database workflows—the MQTT simulator does not replace them, but exposes the same Sparkplug metric contract a future OPC-UA/PLC edge can use.
Permissions: simulator · run for start/stop/scenario; integration · read for status (and the Simulator page uses this for the MQTT connection indicator).

permissions.title: Permissions that touch ML
paragraphs: ai · read: grants AI Insights, AI Studio, Feature Store Monitor, Data Quality views, and related APIs for read-only analysis.

ai · refresh: allows forcing forecast/feature refreshes and destructive cleanup on snapshot tables (for example bulk delete in Feature Data Quality). Grant only to operators who understand training impact.
integrations · read / manage: required for adapter diagnostics and for editing forecast factor JSON; manage is needed to persist factor changes from the hub.

baseline.storage: Platform setting `ai.forecast.factorConfigs` — AI Insights table / Integrations
baseline.precedence: Scope PARK vs ENTITY; entity forecasts also include PARK-scoped rows (no per-park JSON file).

snapshotX.pipeline: Step 2 — adds fixed deltas from weather, calendar, traffic, staffing, capacity
snapshotX.precedence: Not configured via ML factor tables; improve by fixing ingest and snapshot quality.

mlL1.precedence: Default weight; “Current” often resolved from context when no L2/API override (see Help → factor levels).

mlL2.precedence: Park `weightOverride` / `currentValue` beat L1; `current_value` acts as a manual Current override for dynamic codes.

mlL3.pipeline: Step 3 — profile-driven knobs (e.g. elasticity) plus per-asset overrides
mlL3.precedence: Assignment + active overrides beat raw profile defaults — asset-level wins.
